races.name: Title Sponsor Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Kisiyra
runners_data.note: Has raced over 10-14f recently and drops back slightly in trip here; 0 wins 0 places on similar going is a concern, wears headgear (tp), and needs to overcome modest trainer form (T14: 0/9), but a prominent style suits this tactical race shape if Krissy keeps it honest.

runners_data.name: Izzari
runners_data.note: Trainer Jardine in solid form (T14: 4/38) and Cara Tuke claims 5lb, which is a meaningful allowance in a tight handicap; form has been moderate of late (6-4800) but has a win and a place on similar going from a prominent position, and this trip is within range.

runners_data.name: Eagles Dream
runners_data.note: A 316-day absence is the headline concern — has not run since finishing fifth over 14f — and while multiple placed efforts on good ground at 10-12f show ability, returning from such a long layoff in competitive handicap company is a significant ask for a three-year-old.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Josephine Gordon takes the ride for Jardine, who is in good form at T14 (6/33); Mr Lincoln has placed twice on similar going and hit the frame over 16-17f, suggesting stamina is his asset, though dropping back to 1m1f may be sharp enough and he needs a stronger pace than Krissy is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: Dominant recent form (211061) with four wins from nine on similar going makes her the form pick; she is the lone confirmed front-runner and faces no significant early challenge for the lead, though the STYLE_FIT flag reflects the cramped prominent grouping rather than any doubt about her natural racing style.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (b) and has run consistently in the 4-5 bracket over 8-10f on good ground; Tim Easterby sends out a runner with 14 runs over 14 days (T14: 14/100) suggesting a busy yard, but Financer's hold-up style needs more pace than one settled front-runner is likely to generate over this trip.

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners a horse who has recently won (1) and been placed (2) over 8-9f on good ground; David O'Meara in fair form (T14: 6/53), and a prominent racing style over a slightly longer trip than her best form suggests she will travel well but may be tested for toe in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Bellasio
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 8f and has placed three times, suggesting consistent ability at a modest level; a natural front-runner by inclination, she has been pushed back into midfield here simply because Krissy occupies the lead and others ahead of her in the map cannot all secure their position — that positional compromise tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Jewel Maker
runners_data.note: At 11 years old the oldest runner in the field, and recent form (9-0748) is uninspiring; an eleven-year-old with a win and two places on similar going across 15 runs is experienced but declining, and the fact that this genuine front-runner cannot secure a forward pitch in this field compounds the challenge of finding a route into the race.

races.paceDynamic: Krissy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner handicap and, crucially, is unlikely to face any meaningful early pressure — she can dictate a comfortable, controlled gallop across the 1m1f trip on good-to-firm ground at Carlisle. Bellasio and Jewel Maker are genuine prominent types by nature but both have been redistributed to midfield in the race map, as there is simply insufficient room for all the forward-travelling horses to claim their preferred position; Krissy is by far the most likely to secure the rail and the lead. With one horse setting a sustainable, uncontested tempo, the race is unlikely to be truly end-to-end, which historically at Carlisle over this trip on fast ground favours horses who can travel in the first three or four and quicken from a handy position rather than those making up large amounts of ground from the rear. Prominent-to-midfield stalkers with proven form on good-to-firm ground are the profile to focus on, with true hold-up horses facing the biggest ask if the pace is not genuinely strong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Krissy Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy bowls along at a comfortable clip and none of the prominent horses can sustain a challenge turning for home, allowing her to quicken and hold on.
scenarios.body: If Krissy bowls along at a comfortable clip and none of the prominent horses can sustain a challenge turning for home, allowing her to quicken and hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy sets only a modest pace and one of the genuine prominent types tracks her through the race before asserting in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Krissy sets only a modest pace and one of the genuine prominent types tracks her through the race before asserting in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely stronger than expected and the field strings out, giving Mr Lincoln or Eagles Dream time and space to close from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely stronger than expected and the field strings out, giving Mr Lincoln or Eagles Dream time and space to close from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Midrace
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy goes off hard early and comes back to the field, creating a scrambling finish and handing an advantage to a prominent horse who switches off well.
scenarios.body: If Krissy goes off hard early and comes back to the field, creating a scrambling finish and handing an advantage to a prominent horse who switches off well.

watchPoints.text: Krissy's ability to get an uncontested lead unchallenged from the off is the single biggest race-shaping factor — watch whether Bellasio or Jewel Maker's riders elect to contest the early pace despite their redistribution, which would fundamentally change the scenario probabilities.

Eagles Dream has been absent for 316 days and is returning from a layoff that spans the winter; watch how she moves in the early part of the race and whether she travels with her usual fluency — a stiff Carlisle track will quickly expose any ring-rustiness.

Mr Lincoln ran just 15 days ago and drops significantly in trip from his last outing (16f); watch whether he can settle behind the early pace and still have the finishing speed to challenge over the shorter distance on fast ground.

The 5lb claims on Cara Tuke (Izzari) and Lexie Clarkson (Eagles Dream) and Miss Kayleigh Williams (Krissy) could all be influential in such a narrow handicap — watch whether the weight advantage translates into the prominent horses having more left in the tank in the final furlong.

Good-to-firm conditions confirmed for the 6:09 at Carlisle — watch for any late going updates closer to race time, as a drying track in early evening can quicken further and would most benefit Krissy and the proven fast-ground performers like Hostility.

races.name: Style Awards Fashion Finale Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up horse who genuinely operates from the rear, has placed four times in fifteen similar-going runs, and arrives just five days after his last start — the short turnaround is worth monitoring, though his Good ground record is solid and the flat Carlisle mile is within his scope.

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with recent form showing a pair of placings, genuinely wants to race off the pace but is squeezed into a midfield mapping here by the volume of hold-up types — her sim-going record of eight runs yielding no wins and two places on similar ground tempers enthusiasm despite the positive STYLE_FIT adjustment being modest.

runners_data.name: Captain Pickles
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and clear pace-controller, she has won three times in seven recent starts predominantly on Standard ground and arrives after a 54-day absence, making fitness the one note of caution; on form she maps perfectly to the shape she creates, but the style-fit tag reflects she is elevated from her natural lead role only marginally.

runners_data.name: Book Of Life
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who has placed twice in recent outings and arrives 17 days fresh, with a Good to Firm record of just one placing from fifteen sim-going runs — best drawn to challenge Captain Pickles early and let the race come to her in the straight.

runners_data.name: Mertoun
runners_data.note: The form horse in the field on paper — a recent winner over eight furlongs on Good ground, second on Good before that, and rated highest of the field at OR 62; the three-year-old holds a strong position in similar-going runs and is clearly the one to beat if switching off properly from the rear.

runners_data.name: Top Gun Tina
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has recorded no wins and no places across four recent Similar-going appearances, arrives after a 75-day break which is the longest layoff in the field, and while naturally a hold-up horse, finds herself mapped to midfield given the depth of closers — the absence and flat recent form make this an uphill task.

runners_data.name: Wheres The Crumpet
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran who naturally wants to race from the rear but is absorbed into midfield here by the logjam of hold-up types; the form string of 378009 includes a non-completion and the last five runs show finishes between seventh and eleventh — best placed as a negative in the pace analysis.

runners_data.name: Shoptilyoudrop
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with the headgear flag (hg:p) suggesting a blinkers-related angle and a form string of placings and mid-pack finishes on Soft and Standard; naturally a hold-up type pushed into midfield on this map, and with no wins and no sim-going places, she represents a low-probability runner in most scenarios.

runners_data.name: Sanny Doo
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying the lightest weight in the field at 131lbs, with a hg:p headgear flag and recent form dominated by mid-to-back finishes; naturally a hold-up type redistributed to midfield, with three from six sim-going runs showing respectable positioning but no wins — the youth and lighter burden give a trace of intrigue over the flat mile.

runners_data.name: Can I Kiss You
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner in the jockey field, making this horse's participation uncertain — she has one place from eight Good-ground runs at this trip, and if declared her record suggests she typically finishes mid-to-back; note her participation status before race-time.

races.paceDynamic: Captain Pickles is the sole confirmed front-runner in this ten-runner handicap over a flat Carlisle mile on Good to Firm ground, and with no genuine rival prepared to dispute the lead, she faces an entirely uncontested passage through what figures to be a comfortable, self-regulated gallop. The pace is therefore likely to be honest but not gruelling — Captain Pickles can dictate every fraction, control the tempo from the front, and dictate the shape of the race without ever being put under pressure from behind. This race shape strongly favours hold-up or prominent horses with the ability to finish powerfully off a sustainable pace, particularly those with proven form on Good to Firm ground and over this distance — Mertoun, who brings both attributes, and Book Of Life, who can race prominently in support, are ideally positioned. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Wheres The Crumpet, Top Gun Tina, Shoptilyoudrop, and Sanny Doo are all natural hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield, meaning only Mertoun and Wrist Art are likely to operate as true closers from their natural position.

scenarios.title: Captain Pickles Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Pickles secures the lead unchallenged and dictates a steady-to-fair gallop throughout, allowing her to travel well into the straight.
scenarios.body: If Captain Pickles secures the lead unchallenged and dictates a steady-to-fair gallop throughout, allowing her to travel well into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Finishers Catch Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is more generous than expected and Captain Pickles is taken on by a prominent challenger, creating enough tempo for genuine hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: If the pace is more generous than expected and Captain Pickles is taken on by a prominent challenger, creating enough tempo for genuine hold-up horses to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Pickles is tracked closely by Book Of Life and the pair pull clear of a fractured midfield that fails to organise a coherent challenge.
scenarios.body: If Captain Pickles is tracked closely by Book Of Life and the pair pull clear of a fractured midfield that fails to organise a coherent challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsiders Exploit Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of multiple hold-up horses into midfield causes interference or bunching turning for home, opening a gap for an opportunistic mover.
scenarios.body: If the redistribution of multiple hold-up horses into midfield causes interference or bunching turning for home, opening a gap for an opportunistic mover.

watchPoints.text: Captain Pickles — if she misses the break or is slow to stride after 54 days off, the race loses its only confirmed pace-setter and the shape collapses entirely, making a messy, falsely-run affair far more likely.
Can I Kiss You is listed as a non-runner in the jockey field — confirm declaration status before the off, as a withdrawal changes the runner count and may marginally affect pace dynamics.

Mertoun carries the highest rating (OR 62) and comes off a recent win on identical Going, making her the form horse — if she settles cleanly in the early stages, the probability strongly shifts toward Scenario A delivering her as the winner.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Wheres The Crumpet, Top Gun Tina, Shoptilyoudrop, Sanny Doo) all mapped to midfield creates a congestion risk turning out of the back straight — jockeys on Mertoun and Wrist Art should be watched for traffic problems in the final quarter-mile.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed across all Carlisle races today — horses flagged with Standard (STA) form as their primary experience, particularly Top Gun Tina and Wheres The Crumpet, face an unfamiliar surface and should be downgraded accordingly.

races.name: Sheila Petch Appreciation Handicap (For Professional Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Bravo Zulu
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with proven placed form at 8f on Good ground (six runs at the trip or further) and a 15-day turnaround for a yard firing at 3/22 in the past fortnight; needs a stronger pace than Calyxoh alone is likely to generate, which is the key concern here.

runners_data.name: Inspired
runners_data.note: Taryn Langley (claiming 5lb) rides for the in-form K R Burke stable (8/45 T14); travels prominently and that suits this controlled-pace shape perfectly, though her sim-going record of just 0W0P at 8f on similar ground is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who gets a clear lead here and sets a comfortable tempo; her recent form (09 in last two) and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 suggest she is effective only when allowed to dominate, and on Good To Firm she should get away clean — the question is whether she can sustain it.

runners_data.name: Jannas Journey
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old has solid sim-going credentials (2W3P in 10 comparable runs) and races prominently, placing her ideally to track Calyxoh and strike turning for home; Lauren Young claims 5lb and the yard is active at 9/46 in the past 14 days.

runners_data.name: Benacre
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston runner with a clean record at 7f on Good (0W2P in six comparable runs); naturally a prominent racer but the crowded pace map means she is unlikely to secure her ideal berth — Joanna Mason will need to be creative positionally, and that friction tempers her chance.

runners_data.name: The Green Man
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran with genuine placed form at 7f on similar surfaces, including three placings at Southwell and a recent fourth at Carlisle; front-running by nature but pushed back into a mid-race role here given the traffic ahead — his STYLE_FIT of 0.91 reflects the positional compromise, and Josephine Gordon's task is to find cover without losing too much ground.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's progressive hold-up type has finished placed in five of her last five runs at 8f on Good, making her a fascinating runner if the pace suits; Faye McManoman rides and the horse is fresh off a 10-day break for a trainer bagging 14/100 recently — needs more tempo than Calyxoh alone may supply.

races.paceDynamic: Calyxoh is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on Good To Firm ground over Carlisle's flat mile, should slide into an uncontested lead without meaningful pressure from the gate. Inspired and Jannas Journey are the genuine prominent types likely to track close behind, with Benacre and The Green Man — both natural prominent racers — unable to fully secure their preferred positions in a field that has more speed than the map can accommodate, meaning one or both will be shuffled wider or further back than ideal. The resulting shape is a single-pacemaker affair at a controlled, even tempo that will not stretch the field early and is unlikely to produce a truly end-to-end test. That controlled pace over a flat mile in good-to-firm conditions strongly favours horses who can travel prominently just off the leader and kick off the bend — the stalking prominent profile is the primary beneficiary, with hold-up horses needing a tempo injection that is unlikely to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Calyxoh's lead is uncontested but her recent form reads 09 in two starts — if she stops quickly in the final two furlongs, Inspired and Jannas Journey are the immediate dangers to pounce.

Benacre and The Green Man are both natural prominent types who cannot both get to the front; watch the early stages for crowding or a wide passage that costs either of them energy and position before the race truly begins.

Barley has a remarkable record of five placings from five at 8f on Good but is a hold-up type entirely dependent on the pace — if Calyxoh idles, Barley's closing run may flatten out inside the final furlong.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for this race (7:09 slot), faster than the stated Good — any horse with a going concern on quick surfaces should be reassessed, particularly those who have only placed on softer variants of Good.

races.name: Helen Stewart Appreciation Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Junkyard Dog
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for Iain Jardine whose recent form shows modest placing efforts in Soft ground company; the switch to Good to Firm is a positive flag on sim-going evidence (6/15, one win), and Cara Tuke's 5lb claim eases the burden, but from the back in a field where tempo is controlled by one horse, covering ground late remains the central challenge.

runners_data.name: Alpine Sierra
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's consistent mare has won three of her last five runs including back-to-back wins at 11-12f on Good ground, making this trip and surface combination her comfort zone; she is the controlling force in this race and Lauren Young simply needs to avoid a pressured fractions scenario to keep her chance intact, though a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 notes she is nudged slightly out of her preferred role on this map.

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this hold-up type for the Coward yard who have just one run in the past 14 days, suggesting a steadier campaign approach; the mare's second at Haydock over 12f on Good is the standout piece of recent form and 1m3f on Good to Firm suits, though she will need Alpine Sierra to have done genuine work up front before Mason can launch her challenge.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: Placed twice on Good ground in recent starts — including second at Sandown — and the headgear note (t: tongue tie) is worth registering for stamina management over this trip; her true running style is hold-up but she appears on the map in midfield due to redistribution, meaning she will likely race closer to her natural rear position rather than tracking the leaders, which tempers the scenario probability where she needs to be prominent.

runners_data.name: V Twelve
runners_data.note: Martin Todhunter's seven-year-old is returning from an 87-day absence (56 days since jockey change) and that layoff is a material flag in a field where fitness levels matter; Josephine Gordon is an experienced claimer who will manage the hold-up style, but V Twelve's best recent form came on Soft or Heavy ground and the Good to Firm surface is an additional concern, making this the most speculative runner in the field despite the redistributed midfield placement.

races.paceDynamic: Alpine Sierra is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a five-runner field, Lauren Young can dictate an unchallenged, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m3f at Carlisle. The remaining four runners — Junkyard Dog, Valley Of Flowers, Covert Legend, and V Twelve — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the pace is entirely in Alpine Sierra's hands and there is no forcing element to disturb her rhythm. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the pace map can place at the rear; Covert Legend and V Twelve are redistributed to midfield on the map but are true come-from-behind horses who are unlikely to secure a naturally prominent pitch in this shape. This race shape heavily favours front-runners and prominent racers who can control tempo and kick clear in the straight, with hold-up horses dependent on Alpine Sierra setting a strong enough clip to create the gaps they need from further back.

scenarios.title: Alpine Sierra Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Alpine Sierra bowls along at a measured pace and the hold-up brigade cannot produce a decisive late challenge.
scenarios.body: If Alpine Sierra bowls along at a measured pace and the hold-up brigade cannot produce a decisive late challenge.

scenarios.body: If Alpine Sierra sets a genuinely strong gallop that burns her out in the final furlong and the closers sweep past.

scenarios.trigger: If Covert Legend or V Twelve, mapped forward from their natural hold-up role, travel well in mid-division and produce an earlier sustained run than usual.
scenarios.body: If Covert Legend or V Twelve, mapped forward from their natural hold-up role, travel well in mid-division and produce an earlier sustained run than usual.

scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Alpine Sierra misses the break or suffers interference and no horse assumes command early, scrambling the pace entirely.
scenarios.body: If Alpine Sierra misses the break or suffers interference and no horse assumes command early, scrambling the pace entirely.

watchPoints.text: Alpine Sierra's early lead — watch whether Lauren Young is able to stride out unchallenged from flag fall or whether any of the hold-up horses' jockeys push forward unexpectedly to unsettle her rhythm in the first two furlongs.

V Twelve's fitness after an 87-day break is the key unknown; if she travels strongly through the early stages under Josephine Gordon it suggests she has come back well, but if she weakens out of contention from 3f out the layoff has told.

Covert Legend's ground — she has placed consistently on Good but her three previous wins all came on Standish or tighter surfaces; watch for any signs of laboured movement on this Good to Firm strip that could signal the quicker ground is against her.

Junkyard Dog's form has been recorded almost exclusively on Soft or Heavy ground; the sim-going data shows only one win from 15 on similar conditions, so watch whether Cara Tuke asks for her effort earlier than usual to compensate for any doubt about the surface.

Joanna Mason on Valley Of Flowers — Mason is one of the sharpest tactical jockeys in this field and in a small-field race where timing is everything, watch whether she positions closer than the hold-up tag would suggest, potentially tracking Alpine Sierra from the second furlong to reduce the ground she needs to make up late.

races.name: Caledonia Park Stylish Stayers Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Laravie
runners_data.note: Boasts a powerful recent record over staying trips in good ground — four wins from last five including two over 16-17f — and visored, she meets this course and distance test in fine form; racing prominently is natural but the style-fit tag suggests she is placed fractionally out of her optimal position, which marginally tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Tarbat Ness
runners_data.note: Held up in a tongue strap and placed at this course before, though her sim-going record (0W2P from 15 attempts) suggests she rarely wins in these conditions; trainer John Berry has had a quiet recent spell (0 from 3 over 14 days) and she has been consistent without threatening.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's mare is the most interesting hold-up profile in the race — a winner twice on good ground over staying trips and placed off soft, she has strong course-and-distance evidence and Josephine Gordon's level of experience helps; needs a strong enough gallop to make the ground up but has the form to land this if the tempo suits.

runners_data.name: Rupert The Prince
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' four-year-old has a genuine prominent-racing profile but is mapped to midfield given Laravie's natural occupation of the lead — his best form includes a 2m1f placed effort on good ground but his recent string (0-3-4-0 in the last four) shows he is struggling to win; the positional compromise is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Animato
runners_data.note: Fitted in a tongue-piece and held up by nature, Donald McCain's mare has been beaten in soft conditions recently and steps up on going today — a true hold-up runner that the race map can only show in midfield because there are more closers here than positions; her sim-going record (0W0P from 15) is a worry and the redistribution reduces her scenario probability.

runners_data.name: Arctic Fox
runners_data.note: A decade-old veteran for Martin Todhunter who has placed twice over 14f on good ground but struggles over the longer 16f+ trips — the step to 2m1f on quick ground is a stamina question, and his trainer has had no runners in the last 14 days; hold-up style is genuine but he needs pace to close into.

races.paceDynamic: Laravie is the one confirmed front runner here and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, she is expected to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable gallop over this 2m1f trip on good-to-firm ground at Carlisle. That uncontested lead creates a sit-and-sprint shape — a measured tempo that keeps the field together into the straight and rewards those able to pick up from close to the pace rather than those requiring a true searching gallop to reel the leader in. The field does contain more prominent types than can all occupy their natural position: Rupert The Prince and Animato are genuine pace-prominent or hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because Laravie fills the lead unchallenged, meaning neither will likely get the position their form profile demands. The dominant tactical verdict is that this pace shape favours prominent racers and adaptable off-pace types who can track Laravie comfortably and produce a finish from a close-enough position — true hold-up horses needing a strong tempo to close into are disadvantaged.

watchPoints.text: Laravie's early behaviour in the stalls and break from the gate is critical — if she misses the break or is shuffled back, the entire race shape loses its anchor and scenarios shift sharply toward chaos.

Rupert The Prince and Animato are both naturally inclined to race closer than the map shows — watch the first two furlongs to see whether either pushes forward to challenge Laravie for prominent ground, which could inject unplanned pressure and quicken the early tempo.

Cascade Hall's chance is heavily contingent on tempo — if the pace is genuinely slow, her hold-up style becomes a liability; watch whether Lauren Young decides to push forward earlier than expected to avoid being stranded.

Good-to-firm ground is confirmed across all races at Carlisle today — any horse with a soft-ground preference (Animato's recent three runs have all been on soft) may find conditions less forgiving than their recent form suggests.

races.name: Caledonia Park Designer Dash Handicap (For Pro-Am Female Jockeys)

runners_data.name: Another Investment
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Nigel Tinkler whose form-string shows chronic late fading — six recent runs produce mostly double-digit finishes, and the ⚠ fade flag is a real concern; 14 days fresh and carries top weight at 149lbs, all of which compounds the challenge.

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old arrives here off a win (form: 791, most recent a 1) which is the headline, but that victory came on Soft ground and her only run on Good saw a seventh — the going switch needs to prove no barrier; Lauren Young takes the ride for a trainer firing at 6/36 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: No Return
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's hold-up type has placed four times from fifteen similar-going runs and stays the trip well, but her last six outings show nothing better than fourth; Joanna Mason is a strong jockey booking and a 24-day break could mean she arrives fresh, though consistency remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Lumenbourg
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's five-year-old is the lone confirmed pace-setter and wears a visor; her style-fit tag reflects that this Prominent role is slightly outside her natural comfort zone — four of five similar-going runs produced placed efforts but no wins on Good, and she is asked here to hold off a chasing pack.

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's four-year-old has won twice at this exact course-distance-going combination and is arguably the most form-boosted horse in the field — however, her true hold-up style means she has been shifted to midfield on the map because the field is overloaded with closers who cannot all find space at the rear; Josephine Gordon is a quality booking.

runners_data.name: Sherlock
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's four-year-old is the most naturally placed horse behind the leader — prominent style, consistent placed efforts at 6f on Good (two seconds, two fourths in five recent), wears a bridon, and freshness off just nine days is not a concern for this yard; the most structurally suited profile in the field to this pace shape.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old has been rerouted to midfield despite being a genuine hold-up type — her last six runs are all placed-or-near misses but she has never broken her duck, and the 7/98 trainer stat over 14 days flags volume rather than a hot streak; Laura Pearson rides and the hood (p) suggests concentration issues.

runners_data.name: Too Much
runners_data.note: David Thompson's six-year-old is a natural closer whose only similar-going win was at 5f and whose form on Good is thin (2/15 runs); redistributed from the back of the field to midfield because the hold-up contingent is too large to accommodate naturally, and a trainer at 0/7 over 14 days provides little confidence.

runners_data.name: Maui Breeze
runners_data.note: Wilf Storey's four-year-old sports a hood (p) and has not won in fifteen runs on comparable going, with a highest finish of fifth; shifted from a genuine back-of-pack position because of field redistribution, she faces a step back to 6f from longer trips and the trainer sits at 0/3 over the past fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: Lumenbourg is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, on Good to Firm ground at Carlisle over 6f, is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without any genuine challenger pressing for the lead. With no other horse likely to dispute early, the pace will be honest but controlled rather than truly searching, meaning those who race prominently behind Lumenbourg — particularly Sherlock, who has the form figures to track and pounce — are ideally placed to capitalise. The majority of the field consists of true hold-up horses: Invincible Ruby, Fan Mail, Too Much, and Maui Breeze have all been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field is packed with rear-end types who cannot all find their natural late position, and those who do settle deepest risk finding the pace insufficient to fully reel in a front-running winner on this flat track. The tactical verdict is clear: a prominent racing style, tracking the front-runner and hitting the rising ground into the Carlisle straight with cover, is the profile this race shape most strongly favours.

watchPoints.text: Sherlock's early positioning is pivotal — if he slots directly behind Lumenbourg in the first furlong, he controls the race from the prime stalking spot and becomes the main danger to the front-runner throughout.

Invincible Ruby's jockey Josephine Gordon will need to decide whether to hunt up early rather than trust a late run — on a flat track with moderate pace, her natural deep hold-up position may leave her with too much to do, so watch her placement out of the stalls.

Lumenbourg's visor is headgear worn for a reason — if she shows any signs of dwelling or racing freely and burning too bright in the first two furlongs, the controlled gallop scenario collapses and the race shape changes entirely.

Fan Mail's hood and previous form suggest she can be reluctant to fully commit; Laura Pearson will need to produce a positive, hands-and-heels ride from early on if Fan Mail is to make any impact from a redistributed midfield slot.

The Good to Firm going confirmed across all six races on the card is genuine and consistent — horses who have winning or placed form specifically on Good going (Invincible Ruby twice, Sherlock twice) carry a meaningful surface edge over those whose best runs came on Soft.
